author_or_account: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
title: US Consumer Inflation Expectations Decrease Slightly
discussion_signal: The New York Fed post links its August 2026 Survey of Consumer Expectations and says medium-term inflation expectations decreased slightly while unemployment expectations reached their highest level since April 2020. Comments identify the important split: households may see a weaker job market and still have relatively stable inflation expectations, with possible implications for later credit performance. The post and comments do not establish realized unemployment, delinquency, or consumption outcomes.
linked_research_question: When households expect spending to grow faster than income while job and credit confidence weaken, does the adjustment appear first in substitution, borrowing, missed payments, or reduced discretionary demand?
limits: The post reports expectations rather than realized spending, unemployment, or delinquency
Commentary about future credit performance is a hypothesis, not observed evidence
The survey does not by itself identify which households finance the spending gap
